commitResults.messageBody:
Task lists exist only in memory, so users lose all tasks when Rene exits.

Add text-file storage that loads tasks on startup and saves every
successful list mutation. Use a relative default path and create missing
directories so the application works on a fresh checkout.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add UI tests for task persistence
commitResults.messageBody:
Persistence can regress even when single-session command behavior still
works.

Add consecutive save-and-load cases that cover every task type and list
mutation. Give the existing cases isolated data files so repeated test
runs remain deterministic.

Task numbers are current list positions, so deleting a task shifts later
tasks forward. Without clear feedback, marking the new task 1 can look
like it marks the removed task.

Explain renumbering after deletion and add UI cases for empty lists,
shifted positions, and invalid delete arguments.

Deadline due dates are strings, so Rene accepts impossible dates and
cannot format them consistently.

Store deadlines as LocalDate, parse ISO input, and display dates with an
English month name. Keep ISO values in the data file so saved deadlines
can be reconstructed exactly.

Date handling adds format and calendar validation that the existing UI
plan does not cover.

Use ISO deadline inputs throughout the plan. Add focused cases for leap
days, impossible dates, wrong formats, and restart persistence.

Rene currently combines input/output, command parsing, and task-list
management in one class. That makes responsibilities hard to isolate and
change.

Introduce Ui, Parser, and TaskList collaborators, and reduce Rene to
application coordination. Keep console behavior unchanged so the refactor
does not alter existing user workflows.

The chatbot now separates user interaction, parsing, persistence, and
task-list management. Merge the verified refactor so subsequent structural
increments start from the same working behavior.

All classes currently occupy the default package, which hides the
boundaries introduced by the OOP refactor.

Group command, exception, storage, task, and UI classes below the rene root
package. Update the console test commands to compile the package tree and
launch Rene by its fully qualified name.

The source tree now reflects Rene's logical command, storage, task, and UI
boundaries. Merge the tested package structure before adding the Gradle build
configuration that depends on the fully qualified main class.

The project currently relies on manual Java compilation. Bring in the
course-provided Gradle wrapper and build configuration as the supported base
for automated builds, runs, tests, and packaging.

The course Gradle branch targets the template's original main class, so its
run task cannot start the packaged Rene application.

Point the application plugin at rene.Rene and update the console test plan to
compile through Gradle. This makes Gradle the single build path for later
JUnit and JAR increments.

commitResults.messageTitle: Test parsing, storage, and task lists
commitResults.messageBody:
Core command parsing, persistence, and task-list state changes currently
rely only on end-to-end console tests. Failures in those areas are harder to
localize and edge cases can be missed.

Add focused JUnit tests for valid and invalid parsing, storage round trips and
malformed data, task status transitions, deletion, bounds, and immutable
snapshots. These tests cover three independent classes through Gradle.

The project now has focused JUnit coverage for its core parsing, storage,
and task-list logic. Merge the verified tests so future changes can detect
unit-level regressions alongside console regressions.

commitResults.messageTitle: Name the executable JAR after Rene
commitResults.messageBody:
The Shadow configuration still uses the starter template's Duke name even
though the executable launches Rene.

Publish the fat JAR as rene.jar so the distributable matches the application.
The generated archive contains the rene.Rene main class and runs from an empty
directory with java -jar.

The Gradle build now produces a verified executable fat JAR named for Rene.
Merge the packaging configuration so the distributable can be reproduced with
the shadowJar task.

The package tree separates several concerns, but readers currently need to
inspect its classes to understand each package's role.

Add package-level Javadocs for application coordination, commands, errors,
storage, tasks, and console interaction.

Generated API documentation reports gaps for public enum constants and the
Parser constructor. Those gaps make otherwise documented types appear
incomplete.

Describe every public command marker, command type, task status, task type,
and Parser construction point so the Javadoc task finishes without warnings.

commitResults.messageTitle: Align source with Java coding standard
commitResults.messageBody:
Several switch labels are not indented relative to their switch blocks, and
Javadoc tag descriptions omit the required punctuation. Parser also exposes
an undocumented implicit constructor.

Indent switch branches consistently, punctuate parameter and return
information, and make the documented Parser constructor explicit. Keep every
source line within the 120-character hard limit.

Users cannot narrow a long task list to descriptions containing a keyword.

Add a find command that searches descriptions without case sensitivity and
preserves result order, status, and type-specific details. Reject blank
keywords and cover matching, nonmatching, metadata-only, and mixed-case
scenarios with JUnit and console tests.

The public API and package tree now have complete generated documentation.
Merge the independently verified Javadocs first so later parallel branches can
be reconciled against a documented base.

The independent style pass aligns switch indentation and Javadoc tags with
the prescribed Java standard. Merge it after the documentation branch and
retain the complete public API comments from both branches.

The find feature was developed independently from documentation and style
changes. Reconcile the parallel work so task search retains its tests while
the resulting source remains documented and standards-compliant.

commitResults.messageTitle: Configure Checkstyle for automated style checks
commitResults.messageBody: Use the course-recommended rules so Gradle can detect Java coding standard violations consistently. Add a defensive default switch case required by the configured checks.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add a JavaFX interface for Rene
commitResults.messageBody: Let users manage tasks through a responsive FXML-based chat window while preserving the console entry point for automated testing. Share command responses between both interfaces and package JavaFX dependencies for Windows, macOS, and Linux.

commitResults.messageTitle: Use varargs to compose multiline responses
commitResults.messageBody: Centralize newline joining in the console formatter so response methods can supply exactly the lines they need without repeated string concatenation.

commitResults.messageTitle: Close the GUI when the user enters bye
commitResults.messageBody: Preserve the command-line exit workflow in the JavaFX interface so users can close Rene without reaching for window controls.
Bring the GUI's typed bye command in line with the console exit behavior.

Strengthen Rene's visual hierarchy with a branded header, clearer message cards, sender labels, command hints, and a focused composer. Constrain decorative controls and let the scroll pane own vertical overflow so avatars retain their shape and multiline responses remain readable as conversations grow.

The command dispatcher and task list depend on non-null objects and on task indices remaining valid after validation. These assumptions are important but are not visible to maintainers.

Add Java assertions at those internal boundaries so violations fail near their source during development. Keep user-input validation as exceptions because assertions may be disabled at runtime.

The Deadline model names its date field and accessor after the input marker “by”. That terse name makes uses such as getBy() harder to understand without command-syntax context.

Rename the model concept to dueDate and update its consumers. Keep “/by” in the user command and display because that wording remains clear at the interface boundary.

commitResults.messageTitle: Use a stream to find matching tasks
commitResults.messageBody:
Finding tasks is a filter operation over the task collection, but the loop manually creates and fills an intermediate list.

Express the operation as a stream filter and collect an unmodifiable result. This keeps the search criteria prominent while preserving task order and case-insensitive matching.

Users have to infer Rene’s command syntax from error messages or external documentation. That makes the interface harder to discover, especially for commands with required markers.

Add a help command that presents every supported syntax without changing task data. Cover it with unit and console tests, and replace the placeholder user guide with the same command reference.

Clarify deadline date naming
